title: Time-limit the new unemployment insurance to six months
headline: Time-limit the new unemployment insurance to six months: IFS, saves £1.4bn a year.
description: The government proposes to replace new-style jobseeker’s allowance and new-style employment and support allowance with a single contributory unemployment insurance, paid at a higher rate but for a limited time. The IFS Green Budget costs the time limit: once transitional protections expire, twelve months saves around £0.6 billion a year and six months around £1.4 billion. The six-month version is scored here, flat in cash. The people who lose are those with long-term health conditions who would have stayed on the old benefit for longer.

baselinePolicy.text: New-style jobseeker’s allowance and new-style employment and support allowance are contributory benefits with no time limit on the health-related element; the government has proposed a single time-limited unemployment insurance to replace them.

source.quote: the government’s proposal to replace new style jobseeker’s allowance (NS JSA) and new style employment & support allowance (NS ESA) with a single new ‘unemployment insurance’ (UI) benefit

alreadyIncludes: Nothing: the OBR forecast does not yet score the new benefit.

terms.label: The IFS’s steady-state saving from limiting the new unemployment insurance to six months, as a saving
terms.unit: £ million a year, after transitional protections

source.quote: Restricting it to 6 months would save around £1.4 billion a year.

rawSource.note: The IFS’s steady-state figure entered as a negative spending effect and held flat from the start year. The IFS says the saving arrives after transitional protections expire, so the early years would be smaller.

caveats: A steady-state saving: the IFS says it arrives "after any transitional protections had expired", so applying it from 2027-28 overstates the first years.
The IFS’s own arithmetic on a benefit that does not yet exist; the twelve-month version saves around £0.6 billion. Nobody in government has costed the time limit.

Whether the new benefit sits inside or outside the welfare cap depends on how it is classified; jobseeker’s allowance is outside the cap today and contributory employment and support allowance is inside. This card treats the saving as outside the cap.

considerations.text: People with long-term health conditions who would have received new-style employment and support allowance for longer than six months lose; jobseekers gain from the higher rate.

sources.quote: redistribute away from those with long-term health conditions who would have been eligible for the previous benefit for longer than 6 months

considerations.text: Some of those timed out would qualify for means-tested universal credit instead, which claws back part of the saving; the IFS’s figure is a net one.
